flows.period: Primary: LSEG Lipper -- week ended Wed 26 Aug 2026. Cross-check: BofA/EPFR Flow Show (Michael Hartnett), mid-August 2026 reporting.
flows.narrative: Lipper's week-to-26-Aug data shows the first crack in an otherwise resilient inflow picture: global equity funds posted a -$5.87bn outflow, snapping 13 consecutive weeks of inflows, with US equity funds specifically seeing -$22.33bn in net sales. Gold/precious-metals funds bucked the trend hard, drawing +$4.21bn -- a 6-month high -- while global bond funds added a slower +$10.25bn (a 4-week-low pace) and short-term bond funds saw a 7-week-high +$6.29bn, consistent with investors both taking profits in equities and rotating toward safety/gold and shorter duration ahead of Friday's Warsh shock. The prior week (to 19 Aug) had still shown broad-based inflows (equities at a 3-week high, gold +$2.04bn, a 6th straight week). BofA's Flow Show cross-check shows the same defensive tilt at larger EPFR-scope magnitudes: gold funds +$6.3bn in its featured week (biggest since Jan 2026), tech funds' first outflow in 6 weeks (-$700mn) even after annualizing a record $217bn for the year, and the Bull & Bear Indicator climbing to 9.7 (from 9.4) -- the highest since 2021 and squarely in contrarian 'sell' territory. Japan drew a 9th straight week of fund inflows (+$2.6bn) even as JPX's own data (see flows-investors.json) shows foreign investors net-SELLING Japanese cash equities -- a genuine flow-vs-fund-positioning divergence tied to the JGB yield surge.

The largest single-region outflow in the week's data, consistent with BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator hitting 9.7 -- an extremely stretched positioning reading that often precedes a pullback or profit-taking event.
